117|H.R. 1.voting_access: Would have required automatic and same-day registration and fifteen days of early voting in every state; the House passed it 220-210.

117|H.R. 1.scotus_reform: Would have required the Judicial Conference to issue a code of conduct covering Supreme Court justices; the House passed it 220-210.
117|H.R. 1.gov_transparency: Would have made presidential candidates publish ten years of tax returns and widened lobbying registration; the House passed it 220-210.

117|H.R. 1319.child_care: Provided child-care stabilisation funding, supplemental Child Care and Development Block Grant money, and Head Start funding.
117|H.R. 1319.housing_support: Funded emergency rental and homeowner assistance; the House cleared it 220-211, the Senate 50-49.
117|H.R. 1319.healthcare: Expanded Affordable Care Act premium tax credits; the House cleared it 220-211, the Senate 50-49.
117|H.R. 1319.family_support: Raised the child tax credit to $3,000 per child, $3,600 under six, fully refundable; the House cleared it 220-211, the Senate 50-49.
117|H.R. 1319.econ_smallbiz: Funded the Restaurant Revitalization Fund and Shuttered Venue Operators Grants; the House cleared it 220-211, the Senate 50-49.
117|H.R. 1319.public_schools: Created the Elementary and Secondary School Emergency Relief Fund for reopening schools; the House cleared it 220-211, the Senate 50-49.
117|H.R. 1319.healthcare_costs: Expanded ACA premium tax credits for 2021 and 2022 and subsidized COBRA coverage; the House cleared it 220-211, the Senate 50-49.
117|H.R. 1319.tax_middle_class: Expanded the child tax credit; the House cleared it 220-211, the Senate 50-49.
117|H.R. 1319.econ_workers: Extended pandemic unemployment compensation through September 2021; the House cleared it 220-211, the Senate 50-49.
117|H.R. 1319.cost_living: Sent recovery rebates to households and funded emergency rental and utility aid; the House cleared it 220-211, the Senate 50-49.
117|H.R. 1319.national_debt: Roughly $1.9 trillion of pandemic relief, moved through budget reconciliation as emergency spending with no offsetting revenue or cuts.

117|H.R. 1446.gun_safety: Would have enhanced background checks; the House passed it 219-210.

117|H.R. 1808.gun_rights: Would have imposed the Assault Weapons Ban of 2022; the House passed it 217-213.
117|H.R. 1808.gun_safety: Would have enacted an Assault Weapons Ban; the House passed it 217-213.

117|H.R. 2377.gun_safety: Would have created a Federal Extreme Risk Protection Order; the House passed it 224-202.

117|H.R. 3076.gov_services: Ended the Postal Service’s retiree health prepayment and wrote six-day delivery into law; the House cleared it 342-92, the Senate 79-19.
117|H.R. 3076.gov_transparency: Required the Postal Service to publish an online public dashboard of service-performance data, broken down by delivery unit.

117|H.R. 3684.climate_action: Funded clean school buses, a national electric-vehicle charging network, home weatherisation and legacy pollution remediation.
117|H.R. 3684.transit: Reauthorized federal public transportation and funded passenger and freight rail; the House cleared it 228-206, the Senate 69-30.
117|H.R. 3684.infrastructure: Funded roads and bridges, rail, transit, ports, airports and the electric grid; the House cleared it 228-206, the Senate 69-30.
117|H.R. 3684.national_debt: The act’s new spending was only partially offset, so it was scored as adding to the deficit.
117|H.R. 3684.broadband: Created the Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment program for unserved areas; the House cleared it 228-206, the Senate 69-30.
117|H.R. 3684.water: Funded drinking-water and wastewater systems, lead pipe removal and Western water storage; the House cleared it 228-206, the Senate 69-30.
117|H.R. 3684.disaster_resilience: Funded coastal resiliency work, wildfire risk reduction, and hardening of the electric grid against extreme weather.

117|H.R. 4.voting_access: Would have held new photo-ID rules, polling-place closures and voter-roll purges behind federal review; the House passed it 219-212.
117|H.R. 4.states_federal_power: Would have restored Voting Rights Act preclearance and barred states from new covered practices until cleared; the House passed it 219-212.

117|H.R. 4346.tech_innovation: Created the CHIPS for America Fund and authorized NSF, NIST, DOE and NASA research; the House cleared it 243-187, the Senate 64-33.
117|H.R. 4346.strong_defense: Set up the CHIPS for America Defense Fund for microelectronics research; the House cleared it 243-187, the Senate 64-33.
117|H.R. 4346.econ_growth: Expanded federal aid for building and equipping semiconductor plants in the U.S.; the House cleared it 243-187, the Senate 64-33.
117|H.R. 4346.national_debt: The CHIPS funds were appropriated as new spending without offsetting revenue or cuts.

117|H.R. 5323.israel_support: Would have appropriated $1 billion to replace the Iron Dome interceptors Israel expended in May 2021; the House passed it 420-9.

117|H.R. 5376.climate_action: Extended and expanded wind, solar, geothermal and hydropower tax credits; the House cleared it 220-207, the Senate 50-50.
117|H.R. 5376.econ_corp_account: Imposed a 15% minimum tax on corporations above $1 billion and a 1% buyback tax; the House cleared it 220-207, the Senate 50-50.
117|H.R. 5376.lower_taxes: Imposed a 15% minimum tax on the reported income of corporations earning over $1 billion and a 1% excise tax on stock buybacks.
117|H.R. 5376.energy_production: Reinstated Lease Sale 257, ordered sales 258, 259 and 261, and barred federal wind and solar rights-of-way without recent onshore sales.
117|H.R. 5376.healthcare_costs: Extended the enlarged Affordable Care Act premium tax credits through 2025; the House cleared it 220-207, the Senate 50-50.
117|H.R. 5376.health_drug_prices: Required Medicare to negotiate high-spend drug prices and capped insulin cost sharing; the House cleared it 220-207, the Senate 50-50.
117|H.R. 5376.national_debt: Carried a Deficit Reduction subtitle with a corporate minimum tax and IRS enforcement; the House cleared it 220-207, the Senate 50-50.

117|H.R. 5746.voting_access: Would have required same-day registration, two weeks of early voting, no-excuse mail voting and drop boxes; the House passed it 220-203.
117|H.R. 5746.campaign_finance: Would have made election spenders name their donors and curbed super PAC coordination with candidates; the House passed it 220-203.

117|H.R. 7776.strong_defense: Authorized FY2023 Armed Forces end strengths, procurement, operation and maintenance and military pay; the Senate concurred 83-11.

117|H.R. 7910.gun_rights: Would have barred 18-to-20-year-olds from a class of long gun, reclassified bump stocks and banned large-capacity magazines.
117|H.R. 7910.gun_safety: Would have created federal straw-purchase and trafficking offences and required safe storage where a minor could gain access.

117|H.R. 8.gun_safety: Would have extended background checks to the private-sale channel, routing unlicensed transfers through a licensed dealer.

117|H.R. 8404.lgbtq_rights: Repealed the Defense of Marriage Act’s definitions of marriage and spouse; the House cleared it 258-169, the Senate 61-36.
117|H.R. 8404.states_federal_power: Barred anyone acting under state law from refusing to honor another state’s marriage record; the House cleared it 258-169, the Senate 61-36.

117|S. 1605.strong_defense: Authorized FY2022 military end strengths, procurement and construction; the House cleared it 363-70, the Senate 88-11.
117|S. 1605.immig_fentanyl: Made the narcotics report name the top fentanyl source countries and their cooperation; the House cleared it 363-70, the Senate 88-11.
117|S. 1605.israel_support: Set aside up to $200 million to co-produce Israel’s Iron Dome, David’s Sling and Arrow 3; the House cleared it 363-70, the Senate 88-11.

117|S. 2938.healthcare: Directed guidance on Medicaid telehealth and school-based Medicaid services; the House cleared it 234-193, the Senate 65-33.
117|S. 2938.public_schools: Funded school safety programs and school-based mental-health services; the House cleared it 234-193, the Senate 65-33.
117|S. 2938.health_mental: Funded children’s and family mental-health services and paediatric access grants; the House cleared it 234-193, the Senate 65-33.
117|S. 2938.gun_rights: Held under-21 gun sales for review and barred dating partners with abuse convictions; the House cleared it 234-193, the Senate 65-33.
117|S. 2938.gun_safety: Required enhanced checks for buyers aged 18 to 20 and created straw purchasing offences; the House cleared it 234-193, the Senate 65-33.

117|S. 3373.healthcare: Opened VA health care to veterans exposed to burn pits and Agent Orange; the House cleared it 342-88, the Senate 86-11.
117|S. 3373.veterans: Expanded VA benefits and service-connection presumptions for toxic-exposed veterans; the House cleared it 342-88, the Senate 86-11.

118|H.Amdt. 478.israel_support: Would bar the State and foreign operations funds from moving the U.S. Embassy in Israel out of Jerusalem; the House agreed to it 360-67.

118|H.J.Res. 44.gov_regulation: Would have nullified the ATF rule on pistols fitted with stabilizing braces and barred its reissue; it failed in the Senate 49-50.
118|H.J.Res. 44.gun_rights: Would have struck the ATF rule reclassifying braced pistols as short-barrelled rifles; it failed the Senate 49-50.
118|H.J.Res. 44.gun_safety: Would have struck the ATF rule bringing braced pistols under the National Firearms Act; it failed the Senate 49-50.

118|H.R. 192.election_security: Would have barred non-citizens from voting in District of Columbia elections; the House passed it 262-143.
118|H.R. 192.voting_access: Repealed the District law that let non-citizen residents vote in District municipal elections.

118|H.R. 2670.strong_defense: Authorized FY2024 defense procurement, research, military pay and construction; the House cleared it 310-118, the Senate 87-13.
118|H.R. 2670.privacy_rights: Extended section 702 surveillance of targets abroad through April 19, 2024; the House cleared it 310-118, the Senate 87-13.
118|H.R. 2670.israel_support: Set anti-tunnel, counter-drone and refuelling aid for Israel and Iron Dome co-production; the House cleared it 310-118, the Senate 87-13.

118|H.R. 3746.cut_spending: Set discretionary spending caps for FY2024 and FY2025, enforced by sequestration; the House cleared it 314-117, the Senate 63-36.
118|H.R. 3746.energy_production: Ratified all federal approvals for the Mountain Valley Pipeline and barred court review; the House cleared it 314-117, the Senate 63-36.
118|H.R. 3746.permitting_reform: Set page and time limits on environmental impact statements and one lead agency per project; the House cleared it 314-117, the Senate 63-36.
118|H.R. 3746.homeless: Exempted homeless individuals from the SNAP work rule as it raised the age limit to 54; the House cleared it 314-117, the Senate 63-36.
118|H.R. 3746.gov_services: Tightened TANF work rules and raised the SNAP work-requirement age to 54; the House cleared it 314-117, the Senate 63-36.
118|H.R. 3746.edu_college_cost: Ended the federal student-loan payment pause and barred another extension without Congress; the House cleared it 314-117, the Senate 63-36.
118|H.R. 3746.national_debt: Suspended the debt limit through January 1, 2025; the House cleared it 314-117, the Senate 63-36.
118|H.R. 3746.veterans: Exempted veterans from the SNAP work requirement as it raised the age limit to 54; the House cleared it 314-117, the Senate 63-36.

118|H.R. 5009.strong_defense: Authorized FY2025 Pentagon programs, military construction and servicemember pay; the House cleared it 281-140, the Senate 85-14.
118|H.R. 5009.lgbtq_rights: Barred TRICARE from covering treatment for gender dysphoria that could result in sterilisation for a military dependent under 18.

118|H.R. 6126.cut_spending: Would have offset the Israel supplemental by rescinding $14.3 billion of IRS enforcement funding; the House passed it 226-196.
118|H.R. 6126.strong_defense: Would have appropriated emergency defense money to replenish United States stocks drawn down for transfer; the House passed it 226-196.
118|H.R. 6126.israel_support: Would have provided $14.3 billion for Israel’s missile defense, military financing and U.S. stock replacement; the House passed it 226-196.

118|H.R. 7217.strong_defense: Would have funded U.S. military accounts to replace Pentagon stocks; it fell short of two-thirds in the House, 250-180.
118|H.R. 7217.israel_support: Would have provided a $17.6 billion unoffset emergency supplemental for Israel; it fell short of two-thirds in the House, 250-180.

118|H.R. 7888.congress_oversight: Revoked the FBI’s reporting exemption and required regular section 702 reports to Congress; the House cleared it 273-147, the Senate 60-34.
118|H.R. 7888.strong_defense: Reauthorized section 702 foreign-intelligence collection for two years; the House cleared it 273-147, the Senate 60-34.
118|H.R. 7888.privacy_rights: Repealed abouts collection and required FBI approval for U.S.-person section 702 queries; the House cleared it 273-147, the Senate 60-34.

118|H.R. 8034.america_first_fp: Appropriated about $9.2 billion in foreign aid beyond Israel, for disaster, refugee and Sinai needs, unoffset; the House passed it 366-58.
118|H.R. 8034.strong_defense: Would have sent about $7.8 billion to U.S. military accounts, refilling American stocks and Army ammunition; the House passed it 366-58.
118|H.R. 8034.israel_support: Would have funded Iron Dome, David’s Sling, Iron Beam and military financing for Israel; the House passed it 366-58.

118|H.R. 8035.america_first_fp: The standalone Ukraine-aid vote, stripped of the Israel, Indo-Pacific and sanctions divisions that carried the rest of the package.
118|H.R. 8035.restraint: Funded current U.S. military operations in the region and sustained American military support to an active war.
118|H.R. 8035.foreign_balance: Would have funded Ukraine security assistance and replacement of defense articles already transferred; the House passed it 311-112.
118|H.R. 8035.ukraine_policy: Appropriated supplemental security aid for Ukraine, including the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative; the House passed it 311-112.

118|H.R. 815.america_first_fp: Enacted the 118th Congress’s largest foreign-aid appropriation, for Israel, Ukraine and the Indo-Pacific; the Senate concurred 79-18.
118|H.R. 815.restraint: Sustained U.S. military support to two active wars and Pacific deterrence through three security divisions; the Senate concurred 79-18.
118|H.R. 815.iran_policy: Carried Iran-related sanctions in Division D, the 21st Century Peace through Strength Act; the Senate concurred 79-18.
118|H.R. 815.tech_balance: Carried the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, a divest-or-ban rule; the Senate concurred 79-18.
118|H.R. 815.immig_fentanyl: Carried the FEND Off Fentanyl Act, with sanctions and anti-money-laundering steps against fentanyl traffickers; the Senate concurred 79-18.
118|H.R. 815.foreign_balance: Appropriated security assistance across three theatres at once, Israel, Ukraine and the Indo-Pacific; the Senate concurred 79-18.
118|H.R. 815.israel_support: Provided $5.2 billion for Iron Dome, David’s Sling and Iron Beam and $3.5 billion in Israel military financing; the Senate concurred 79-18.
118|H.R. 815.ukraine_policy: Carried the Ukraine security supplemental as Division B of the 2024 national-security package; the Senate concurred 79-18.

118|H.R. 82.social_security: Repealed the Windfall Elimination Provision and Government Pension Offset, raising benefits for public-sector retirees.
118|H.R. 82.cost_living: Increased monthly retirement income for affected teachers, firefighters, police and other public workers.

118|H.R. 8281.election_security: Would have required documentary proof of U.S. citizenship before a state registers a federal voter; the House passed it 221-198.
118|H.R. 8281.voting_access: Would have required proof of citizenship in person at an election office, closing mail registration; the House passed it 221-198.
118|H.R. 8281.states_federal_power: Would have written the proof-of-citizenship rule into federal law for every registration channel a state runs; the House passed it 221-198.

118|H.R. 8369.power_of_purse: Would have barred spending appropriated funds to withhold or cancel delivery of defense articles; the House passed it 224-187.
118|H.R. 8369.israel_support: Would have required the President to deliver to Israel the defense articles Congress had already funded; the House passed it 224-187.

118|S.Amdt. 1354.gun_rights: Prohibited VA reporting of fiduciary determinations to NICS; the Senate agreed to it 53-45.

118|S.Amdt. 1354.veterans: Barred funds for Veterans Affairs to report certain information to NICS for background checks; the Senate agreed to it 53-45.

118|S.J.Res. 111.israel_support: Would have blocked the sale to Israel of tank rounds and 120mm mortar cartridges; the Senate refused to discharge it 18-79.

118|S.J.Res. 113.israel_support: Would have blocked the sale to Israel of JDAM guidance kits and small-diameter bombs; the Senate refused to discharge it 19-78.
